author: derived from ASL-LEX annotations carried in semlex_metadata.csv
why: Unlike the 250-word lexicon, handedness here is NOT hand-written from published
descriptions. Sem-Lex carries the ASL-LEX phonological annotation set per video,
so Sign Type / Nondominant Handshape / Minor Location come with a take count and a
citable source. Every one of the annotated medical words is UNANIMOUS across its
takes, which is what a per-SIGN (not per-video) annotation should look like.
Each row is then checked against the landmarks independently: a class-1 label with
both hands tracked, or a two-handed label with no second hand, is demoted to

classes.1: One-handed. Only the dominant hand is phonemically required.
classes.2s: Two-handed SYMMETRIC (Battison's Symmetry Condition): both hands share the same handshape and both move.
classes.2a: Two-handed ASYMMETRIC (Battison's Dominance Condition): the dominant hand acts on a static passive base, whose handshape is restricted to the unmarked set (B, A, S, 1, 5, C, O). Includes ASL-LEX's 'Asymmetrical Same Handshape' and 'Dominance Violation', which our taxonomy does not separate.

renderer_contract: 🔑 THIS DIFFERS FROM asl_handedness_250.json, AND THAT IS THE POINT.
The 250-word contract says: 'For every word not marked 1, the passive hand's
landmarks DO NOT EXIST in our corpus for any take.' True of GISLR, which records
one hand per participant -- both hands in 1.7% of clips, 0.1% of frames.
FALSE for Sem-Lex. Measured on these 55 words in data_medical/by_word/:
class 1   24 words, 1,765 clips ->  4.1% of frames carry both hand blocks
Two-handed words average 41.8% against GISLR's 0.1%. The 10x separation between
class 1 and the two-handed classes means the tracking INDEPENDENTLY corroborates
these ASL-LEX labels -- neither number was derived from the other.
So for the medical avatar the passive hand is RECORDED, not synthesized. Prefer the
real passive hand; fall back to mirroring (2s) or an unmarked base (2a) only on the
frames where it is absent. passive_hand_recorded_frac is per word, so decide per
word rather than per corpus -- `walk` is 15.5% and still needs synthesis.

conf.high: unanimous ASL-LEX Sign Type over >=20 takes, and the tracking agrees
conf.low: few takes, ASL-LEX disagreement, tracking contradicts the label, or hand-labelled. REVIEW THESE FIRST.

review_status: NOT reviewed by a Deaf signer. ASL-LEX is linguist-annotated, which makes this a better starting point than the 250-word lexicon's hand-written rows -- not a substitute for review. Review conf='low' rows, label_vs_tracking_flags, cross_check_vs_250, and every outside_unmarked_set row first.
licence_note: These class labels are ASL-LEX annotations redistributed through Sem-Lex (CC BY-NC-SA). The medical model is already non-commercial for the same reason, so this file changes nothing about THIS track's shippability. It becomes a live question only if the labels are reused for the 250-word commercial track. A Deaf reviewer must be the one who SETS a shipped label; ASL-LEX only says where to look.

label_vs_tracking_flags.note: ASL-LEX says ONE-handed but both hand blocks are tracked in 45.2% of frames (class-1 words average 4.1%). Either the sign has a two-handed variant in this corpus, or the label is wrong. Review before the renderer trusts '1'.

passive_handshape._why: The passive hand's handshape per two-handed word, and where the dominant hand meets it. Sourced from ASL-LEX Nondominant Handshape / Minor Location rather than guessed. contact_surface is non-null only where Minor Location names a part of the hand or arm; otherwise the sign is located on the body (body_location) or in neutral space.
passive_handshape._fallback: Shapes requested by this vocabulary are B, 1 and 5. All three are measured and usable in handshape_templates.json (agreement_xy 0.131 / 0.150 / 0.153), so there are ZERO live approximations here -- the same as the 250-word set. Only 'O' is unusable and it is never requested.

sit.note: ASL-LEX records 'Dominance Condition Violation' in the Nondominant Handshape field for 63 takes. That is a category, not a handshape: the non-dominant hand acts as dominant. Passive shape UNKNOWN here.
